Education system 1

Understand how Thai schooling works, in Thai. This topic walks the whole ladder — อนุบาล (kindergarten), ประถม (primary), มัธยมต้น (lower secondary) and มัธยมปลาย (upper secondary) up to มหาวิทยาลัย (university) — plus fees, the entrance exam, getting into the faculty you want, and the huge world of เรียนพิเศษ (extra tuition) and กวดวิชา (cram schools). It also covers compulsory ชุดนักเรียน (school uniforms), international schools, and the May-start academic year. All 28 sentences come with native-speed audio, English translations, and word-by-word notes, so it sinks in by ear.

4 มัธยมปลาย…

In Thailand you do three years of upper secondary before university.

Thai schooling runs อนุบาล (kindergarten) → ป.1–6 (ประถม, primary) → ม.1–3 (มัธยมต้น, lower secondary) → ม.4–6 (มัธยมปลาย, upper secondary) → university. Grades are written ป./ม. plus a number, so 'ม.6' is the final pre-university year.
5 ค่าเทอม…

โรงเรียนรัฐบาล=government schoolกับ=andเอกชน=privateต่างกัน=differที่=inค่าเทอม=tuition fees
Thai schools fall into tiers: รัฐบาล (government, low or no fees, often crowded) and เอกชน (private, fee-paying), plus a pricier โรงเรียนนานาชาติ (international) tier teaching in English.
6 ปริญญาตรี…

จุฬาฯ is Chulalongkorn University, Thailand's oldest and most prestigious (the ฯ is an abbreviation mark). A place at a top public university like Chula or Thammasat carries real social weight.

Until a few decades ago many older Thais — especially in the countryside — left school after ป.4, then the end of compulsory education. Free schooling now extends to ม.3.

วิศวะ is the colloquial clip of วิศวกรรมศาสตร์ (engineering). Thais routinely shorten faculty names this way — หมอ for medicine, นิติ for law, บัญชี for accounting.

Cram schools (โรงเรียนกวดวิชา) are a huge private industry: after regular classes, students pay for intensive, exam-focused drilling. เรียนพิเศษ is the broader term for any paid extra tuition; กวดวิชา specifically targets entrance exams.
